title: [Chapitre] I. Vers une géométrie des formes (topologiques) : notes manuscrites (05/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: pages 4–7 build a set-theoretic, point-free axiomatics for a 'modèle d'une forme 1-dimensionnelle', a one-dimensional topological shape such as a graph or curve. The data are a set L of 'lieux' (places), a set S of 'segments', a map I ↦ Ĩ ⊂ L (the places on I) and a map I ↦ ∂I ∈ P_2(L) (the two end-places), with ∂I ⊂ Ĩ.

Axioms from the previous page:
- F1 (sub-segments): for ∂I = {x,y} and each z ∈ Ĩ∖{x} there is a unique sub-segment I_{x,z} with Ĩ_{x,z} ⊂ Ĩ and ∂I_{x,z} = {x,z}.
- F2 (cutting, with 'divisibility'): the interior is non-empty. For an interior z, Ĩ_{x,z} ∩ Ĩ_{y,z} = {z}, and any sub-segment of I ending at z lies on one side.
- Cor 3: the map S_I → P_2(Ĩ), J ↦ ∂J, is (a) injective and (b) hits every pair that meets ∂I.

This page:
- Cor 3(c) treats an interior pair {u,v}, i.e. one with {u,v} ∩ ∂I = ∅. It lists 'equivalent conditions':
  1) there is J ∈ S_I with ∂J = {u,v};
  2) and 3) are order relations: whether v lies on the x-side or the y-side of u, and symmetrically for u relative to v.
  The margin NB writes the chain v ∈ Ĩ_{x,u} ⇔ u ∈ Ĩ_{y,v} ⇔ …. Its content is that the places of a segment carry a linear 'betweenness' order compatible with the two endpoints. He notes that u ≠ v must be said explicitly and defers this ('on y reviendra').
- Cor 4: Ĩ = J̃ ⇒ I = J, so S can be identified with a family of subsets of L. Endpoints are recovered from Ĩ because an interior point cannot be an endpoint of a sub-segment with the same underlying set (F2), and then Cor 3(a) applies.
- F3, the 'axiome des branches': let I, J ∈ S have a common endpoint x. Then there are u ∈ I∖{x} and v ∈ J∖{x} such that either
  - I_{x,u} = J_{x,v}, hence u = v, a common initial germ; or
  - Ĩ_{x,u} ∩ J̃_{x,v} = {x}, so the initial pieces separate at x.
  He corrects u ∈ I°, v ∈ J° to u ∈ I∖{x}, v ∈ J∖{x} 'si on n'introduit pas de condition de divisibilité'. That is, he wants the axioms to cover discrete, combinatorial-graph-like models as well as continua. The NB states that the two alternatives are mutually exclusive.
- Branches and order: the relation R_x, 'there is z with I_{x,z} = J_{x,z}', is an equivalence relation on S_x, the segments with endpoint x. B_x = S_x/R_x is the set of branches at x, and its cardinal is the order of x. The next page continues: order 0 is an isolated place, order 1 an end ('lieu-bout'); regular places are then defined and a gluing axiom F4 is stated.
- Left margin: 'Axiome des branches ⇒ F5' and 'il manque … partie (b) de F3'. A variant F3′ is sketched: for I with ∂I = {x,y} and interior u, v there are w ∈ I_{x,u} and w′ ∈ I_{v,y} with some condition. This is apparently an axiom guaranteeing the order/separation of interior points, i.e. completing Cor 3(c).

Purpose: a synthetic, topology-free axiomatisation of 1-dimensional 'formes', presumably the base case of the 'géométrie des formes' / tame-topology programme. It recovers branch points, valence and ends from a segment calculus.
errors: The definition of R_x is written 'I_{x,z} = I_{y,z}'. This must be a slip for 'I_{x,z} = J_{x,z}' with I, J ∈ S_x; as written it is impossible by F2.

Cor 3(c) is labelled 'conditions équivalentes', but condition 1 (existence of a J with ∂J = {u,v}) already follows from F1 applied to the sub-segment I_{x,u} once v ∈ Ĩ_{x,u}, or to I_{y,u} otherwise. What genuinely needs an axiom is that Ĩ_{x,u} ∪ Ĩ_{y,u} = Ĩ (every interior v lies on one side) and the symmetry of betweenness. Grothendieck himself flags the gap: 'Il manque … partie (b) de F3', and F3′ in the margin.
Transitivity of R_x is asserted, not proved. It needs the comparison of two initial germs inside one segment, i.e. the linear order from Cor 3(c), which is not yet fully established.

Mutual exclusivity of the two alternatives in F3 (the NB) also tacitly uses that two germs I_{x,u}, I_{x,u'} of the same segment meet in more than {x}. This is true, but relies on the same order structure.

ideas.what: Point-free / set-theoretic axiomatics of 1-dimensional shapes via places, segments, underlying sets and endpoints (sub-segment axiom, cutting axiom)
ideas.modern_name: betweenness / arc-system axiomatics; closest relatives are pretrees and arc-systems for dendrites and graphs
ideas.usually_credited_to: Hilbert (order axioms); Ward (1950s, betweenness for trees); Bowditch (pretrees, 1990s); continuum theorists
ideas.where_published: Spirit only: Esquisse d'un programme §5 (topologie modérée) mentions a 'théorie des formes'; this axiomatics is unpublished

ideas.what: Segments determined by their underlying set of places (Cor 4)
ideas.modern_name: arcs as subsets; extensionality of the arc system

ideas.what: Branch axiom F3 and the equivalence relation 'same initial germ' on segments ending at x; branches B_x and order of x = card B_x
ideas.modern_name: germs of arcs at a point (directions/ends at a point); Menger–Urysohn order (valence) of a point
ideas.usually_credited_to: Menger and Urysohn (order of a point in a continuum, 1920s–30s); directions at a point in R-trees (Morgan–Shalen and others)

ideas.what: Deliberately weakening axioms (no divisibility condition) so that discrete combinatorial graphs and continuous 1-dimensional forms satisfy one common axiom system
ideas.modern_name: unified discrete/continuous betweenness structures (cf. pretrees, which include both simplicial and real trees)

missed.claim: Grothendieck began a complete synthetic, topology-free axiomatics of 1-dimensional 'forms', not restricted to trees, with places, segments, branches, order of a point, regular/singular places and gluing. He explicitly left the axiom guaranteeing the linear order of interior points as an open item.
missed.quote: Il manque … partie (b) de F3 … ou (F3'): Soit I ∈ S, … u, v ∈ I°, ∂I = {x,y} … ∃ w ∈ I_{x,u}, ∃ w' ∈ I_{v,y}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Pretree and median-algebra axiomatics handle trees. A comparable axiomatic characterisation of general (finite or locally finite) topological graphs, including cycles, from a segment calculus is not standard. It is a concrete fragment of his 'géométrie des formes' programme that remains undeveloped.

missed.claim: The 'ordre' of a place, defined as the number of germ-classes of segments ending there, reproduces the classical Menger–Urysohn order of a point in continuum theory. It does so purely combinatorially and in a framework meant to cover discrete graphs too (option without divisibility).
missed.quote: l'ensemble des branches en x, son cardinal l'ordre de x … devrait plutôt u ∈ I∖{x}, v ∈ J∖{x} (si on n'introduit pas de condition de divisibilité)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It links continuum theory (dendrites, regular curves), graph theory (valence) and Grothendieck's tame-topology ideas in one axiom system. This bridge is not documented as part of his programme.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but elementary foundational axiomatics; the individual notions (betweenness, germs of arcs, order of a point) are classical. What is notable is that it documents how Grothendieck concretely started the unpublished 'géométrie des formes' in 1986, and that he aimed at a single framework for discrete and continuous 1-dimensional shapes. No deep new theorem appears.
transcription_corrections: Item 2) of Cor 3(c) is more likely 'v ∈ Ĩ_{x,u} ⇔ (non) v ∈ Ĩ_{y,u}', an exclusive alternative, than a plain equivalence. The margin NB reads approximately 'v ∈ Ĩ_{x,u} ⇔ u ∈ Ĩ_{y,v} ⇔ …'.
The definition of R_x reads 'I_{x,z} = I_{y,z}' on the page, but it must mean I_{x,z} = J_{x,z}.
The note 'x ∈ I' near Cor 4 is the beginning of the F3 hypothesis 'x ∈ ∂I ∩ ∂J'.
The right-margin note reads approximately 'devrait plutôt u ∈ I∖{x}, v ∈ J∖{x} (si on n'introduit pas de condition de divisibilité)'.
The left margin includes 'Axiome des branches' and '⇒ F5'.
The final line ends 'Ordre 0 :', continued on the next page as 'lieu isolé'.
